import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 214

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/214](https://www.erdosproblems.com/214)
- [CsTo94] Csizmadia, György and Tóth, Géza, *Note on a Ramsey-type problem in geometry*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1994), 302-306.
- [EGMRSS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Montgomery, P. and Rothschild, B. L. and Spencer, J.
  and Straus, E. G., *Euclidean Ramsey theorems. II*. (1975), 529-557.
- [Ju79] Juhász, Rozália, *Ramsey type theorems in the plane*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979),
  152-160.
-/

open scoped Congruent EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos214

/-- The four vertices of a unit square. -/
def unitSquare : Fin 4 → ℝ² := ![!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]]

/-- Colouring the points of `S` blue and the points of `Sᶜ` red gives a red/blue colouring of
$\mathbb{R}^2$; it is unit-distance-avoiding if no two blue points are distance $1$ apart. -/
def UnitDistanceAvoiding (S : Set ℝ²) : Prop := ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, dist x y ≠ 1

/-- Any unit-distance-avoiding colouring contains a congruent red copy of every set of `n`
points. -/
def HasRedCopies (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set ℝ², UnitDistanceAvoiding S → ∀ K : Fin n → ℝ², Function.Injective K →
    ∃ p : Fin n → ℝ², (∀ i, p i ∈ Sᶜ) ∧ (p ≅ K)

/-- The largest integer `k` such that any unit-distance-avoiding colouring contains a congruent
red copy of every set of `k` points. -/
noncomputable def k : ℕ := sSup {n | HasRedCopies n}

/--
Let $S\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no two points in $S$ are distance $1$ apart. Must the
complement of $S$ contain four points which form a unit square?

The answer is yes, proved by Juhász [Ju79], who proved more generally that the complement of $S$
must contain a congruent copy of any set of four points.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos214.lean"]
theorem erdos_214 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ S : Set ℝ², UnitDistanceAvoiding S →
      ∃ p : Fin 4 → ℝ², (∀ i, p i ∈ Sᶜ) ∧ (p ≅ unitSquare) := by
  sorry

/--
The answer is yes, proved by Juhász [Ju79], who proved more generally that the complement of $S$
must contain a congruent copy of any set of four points.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.juhasz : HasRedCopies 4 := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus [EGMRSS75] had earlier showed that
$3\leq k\leq 10^{12}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.egmrss : 3 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 10 ^ 12 := by
  sorry

/--
Juhász [Ju79] also improved the upper bound to $k\leq 11$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.juhasz_twelve_points : ¬ HasRedCopies 12 := by
  sorry

/--
The upper bound was improved further by Csizmadia and Tóth [CsTo94] to $k\leq 7$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.csizmadia_toth : ¬ HasRedCopies 8 := by
  sorry

/--
The best known bounds currently are
$$4\leq k\leq 7.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_214.variants.bounds : 4 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 7 := by
  sorry

end Erdos214

reformulations.difference: Uses a natural-number supremum to define the largest admissible configuration size.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: HasRedCopies 0 holds, and HasRedCopies is downward closed: extend any smaller configuration by distinct points, apply the larger-size assertion, and restrict the resulting copy. The published finite counterexamples therefore bound the admissible sizes. Consequently the defining set is nonempty and bounded, and its natural-number supremum is its maximum; the unbounded-set default of 0 is unreachable. The nonemptiness, downward closure, and maximum property under the known boundedness hypothesis were proved in scratch Lean.

reformulations.difference: States ¬ HasRedCopies 12 rather than the upper bound k ≤ 11.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Negating HasRedCopies 12 is exactly the existence of a unit-distance-avoiding set S and a distinct twelve-point configuration K such that every congruent copy of K meets S. This is the counterexample formulation of Juhász's result. Since admissible sizes are downward closed and have a maximum, failure at size 12 is equivalent to k ≤ 11. Scratch Lean proves the counterexample equivalence unconditionally, and the bound equivalence under the independently established boundedness hypothesis.

reformulations.difference: States ¬ HasRedCopies 8 rather than explicitly constructing an eight-point counterexample or writing k ≤ 7.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Classically, ¬ HasRedCopies 8 says that some unit-distance-avoiding S and injective eight-point configuration K have every congruent copy intersecting S. After exchanging the color names, this is exactly Csizmadia–Tóth's Theorem 1. Downward closure and the existence of a maximum also make it equivalent to k ≤ 7. Both logical reformulations were checked in scratch Lean, with known boundedness supplied for the maximum-based equivalence.

could_not_verify: Erdos214.erdos_214.variants.bounds: the inequalities 4 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 7 are verified, but the docstring's claim that these remain the best known bounds today could not be confirmed against the blocked live problem page.
review.notes: Checked all four definitions and six theorems. Lean experiments verified the Euclidean side and diagonal distances of unitSquare, injectivity inherited by congruent copies, empty/singleton avoiding sets, sizes 0 and 1, existence of injective configurations of every finite size, and the supremum/counterexample equivalences. The cited four-point proof needed four proof-only compatibility fixes for the available Lean/Mathlib version; the resulting scratch bridge proves both HasRedCopies 4 and the exact main statement with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The reviewed file matches its committed blob and was not modified. Direct access to erdosproblems.com and Juhász's full paper was blocked; the original question and early bounds were checked in EGMRSS75, and Juhász's results in the cited Csizmadia–Tóth paper and linked formalization. The independent problem database records problem 214 as proved, with a Lean proof, consistent with the file.
